5	A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.
6	
7	A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.
8	
9	The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.
10	
11	To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.
12	
13	The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

file.content: The present disclosure relates to clamps that are applied around a pipe, and more particularly to a reusable split clamp whose frame opens on a hinge to receive a pipe that is already in place and whose jaws are advanced onto the pipe by a latch driven cam mechanism.

content.content:
1	Pipework in process plants, buildings, vehicles and drilling installations often has to be gripped by a device that cannot be threaded on from a free end of the pipe. Sensors, monitoring heads, marking tools, small actuators and conduit supports are attached to a run of pipe that is already installed. A clamp intended for that duty is therefore built as a split clamp: a frame that opens, is placed around the pipe transversely, and is closed again.
2	
3	A split frame presents a mechanical problem that a one piece collar does not have, because the tightening motion has to be delivered to a frame that is divided. Where the grip is obtained by drawing the two frame halves toward one another so that the frame itself shrinks onto the pipe, the closing force enters the frame at the split line, and the grip that results depends on the closure hardware and on how far the halves have been drawn together.
4	
5	Where instead the frame is fitted with jaws that are advanced against the pipe one at a time, the grip is taken away from the split line, but the jaws have to be balanced against one another by the operator. If one jaw is advanced further than the others, the pipe is pushed away from the axis of the frame, and the clamp is seated differently each time it is fitted.
6	
7	A clamp whose jaw faces match one nominal pipe diameter also obliges a technician to select the clamp to suit the pipe before working, and a jaw face of fixed curvature meets a pipe of a different diameter along an edge rather than over an area.
8	
9	An operator working with a quick acting latch further has little indication of how hard the clamp has been applied. The latch closes to the same position whether the jaws have only just reached the pipe or have been driven hard against it, so the feel of the latch does not report the load the clamp is carrying, and a reading of pipe diameter reports only the size of the pipe.
10	
11	There is accordingly a need for a split pipe clamp that can be fitted by hand around an in place pipe over a range of diameters, that advances several jaws onto the pipe together rather than one at a time, and that reports mechanically to the operator when the clamping load has reached the intended range.
12

file.content:
Pipework in process plants, buildings, vehicles and drilling installations often has to be gripped by a device that cannot be threaded on from a free end of the pipe. Sensors, monitoring heads, marking tools, small actuators and conduit supports are attached to a run of pipe that is already installed. A clamp intended for that duty is therefore built as a split clamp: a frame that opens, is placed around the pipe transversely, and is closed again.

A split frame presents a mechanical problem that a one piece collar does not have, because the tightening motion has to be delivered to a frame that is divided. Where the grip is obtained by drawing the two frame halves toward one another so that the frame itself shrinks onto the pipe, the closing force enters the frame at the split line, and the grip that results depends on the closure hardware and on how far the halves have been drawn together.

Where instead the frame is fitted with jaws that are advanced against the pipe one at a time, the grip is taken away from the split line, but the jaws have to be balanced against one another by the operator. If one jaw is advanced further than the others, the pipe is pushed away from the axis of the frame, and the clamp is seated differently each time it is fitted.

A clamp whose jaw faces match one nominal pipe diameter also obliges a technician to select the clamp to suit the pipe before working, and a jaw face of fixed curvature meets a pipe of a different diameter along an edge rather than over an area.

An operator working with a quick acting latch further has little indication of how hard the clamp has been applied. The latch closes to the same position whether the jaws have only just reached the pipe or have been driven hard against it, so the feel of the latch does not report the load the clamp is carrying, and a reading of pipe diameter reports only the size of the pipe.

There is accordingly a need for a split pipe clamp that can be fitted by hand around an in place pipe over a range of diameters, that advances several jaws onto the pipe together rather than one at a time, and that reports mechanically to the operator when the clamping load has reached the intended range.

content.content:
1	A reusable split pipe clamp is disclosed in which the ring that drives the jaws is itself split, one segment traveling with each half of the frame, and is made into a working ring by the act of closing the frame.
2	
3	The clamp has a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and joined at a latch end by a releasable latch, so that the frame halves can be swung apart, placed around a pipe, and closed again. Three jaw carriages are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame. Each jaw carriage is slidable in a radial guide of the frame and carries a jaw pad that is mounted on the jaw carriage for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface to the pipe. Because each jaw pad pivots, it bears on the pipe without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.
4	
5	A cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. The cam ring is segmented. A first cam-ring segment is carried by the first frame half and a second cam-ring segment is carried by the second frame half, so each segment stays with its own frame half when the clamp is opened. The first cam-ring segment and the second cam-ring segment have complementary drive faces at the hinge end and complementary drive faces at the latch end. Closing the frame halves brings those complementary drive faces into engagement and couples the cam-ring segments so that they move together as one cam ring about the pipe.
6	
7	Each jaw carriage carries a follower that is received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. The latch carries a wedge. Moving the latch drives the wedge against a ring drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled cam ring through a limited stroke about the pipe. Each oblique slot converts that common rotation into inward travel of its own jaw carriage, so that all of the jaw carriages advance together through the same inward travel. A carriage spring biases each jaw carriage outward, so that releasing the latch retracts the jaw carriages and lifts the jaw pads off the pipe before the frame halves are opened.
8	
9	The latch has a first position in which it holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second, over-center position in which it drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. The two positions separate the act of capturing the pipe from the act of loading the jaws.
10	
11	A force-limiting spring stack lies in the drive path between a latch handle of the latch and the wedge. Once all of the jaw pads have contacted the pipe, further movement of the latch handle toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack rather than forcing one jaw pad farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.
12	
13	An indicator pin is visible on the latch and moves relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing of the latch when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range, giving the operator a mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator reports clamp loading and does not measure pipe diameter.
14	
15	The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, a tool or a conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages.
16	
17	A method of clamping a pipe and a method of releasing the clamp are also disclosed, in which the frame halves are closed about the pipe to couple the cam-ring segments, the latch is moved to the first position and then to the over-center position to rotate the coupled cam ring, and the latch travel that remains after the jaw pads seat is taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.
18

A reusable split pipe clamp is disclosed in which the ring that drives the jaws is itself split, one segment traveling with each half of the frame, and is made into a working ring by the act of closing the frame.

The clamp has a first frame half and a second frame half joined at a hinge end by a hinge and joined at a latch end by a releasable latch, so that the frame halves can be swung apart, placed around a pipe, and closed again. Three jaw carriages are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame. Each jaw carriage is slidable in a radial guide of the frame and carries a jaw pad that is mounted on the jaw carriage for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface to the pipe. Because each jaw pad pivots, it bears on the pipe without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. The cam ring is segmented. A first cam-ring segment is carried by the first frame half and a second cam-ring segment is carried by the second frame half, so each segment stays with its own frame half when the clamp is opened. The first cam-ring segment and the second cam-ring segment have complementary drive faces at the hinge end and complementary drive faces at the latch end. Closing the frame halves brings those complementary drive faces into engagement and couples the cam-ring segments so that they move together as one cam ring about the pipe.

Each jaw carriage carries a follower that is received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. The latch carries a wedge. Moving the latch drives the wedge against a ring drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled cam ring through a limited stroke about the pipe. Each oblique slot converts that common rotation into inward travel of its own jaw carriage, so that all of the jaw carriages advance together through the same inward travel. A carriage spring biases each jaw carriage outward, so that releasing the latch retracts the jaw carriages and lifts the jaw pads off the pipe before the frame halves are opened.

The latch has a first position in which it holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second, over-center position in which it drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. The two positions separate the act of capturing the pipe from the act of loading the jaws.

A force-limiting spring stack lies in the drive path between a latch handle of the latch and the wedge. Once all of the jaw pads have contacted the pipe, further movement of the latch handle toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack rather than forcing one jaw pad farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.

An indicator pin is visible on the latch and moves relative to a fixed edge of a latch housing of the latch when the force-limiting spring stack enters a predetermined compression range, giving the operator a mechanical report that the clamp is loaded within that range. The indicator reports clamp loading and does not measure pipe diameter.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, a tool or a conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages.

A method of clamping a pipe and a method of releasing the clamp are also disclosed, in which the frame halves are closed about the pipe to couple the cam-ring segments, the latch is moved to the first position and then to the over-center position to rotate the coupled cam ring, and the latch travel that remains after the jaw pads seat is taken up by the force-limiting spring stack.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIGS. 2 and 5, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50. The first hinge-end drive face 44 and the second hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 5. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

4	
5	A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

7	A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.
8	
9	The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. 12

# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)

This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.

A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.

A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.

The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.

To install the clamp, an operator opens the latch, swings the frame halves apart, places them around a pipe, closes the frame, moves the latch to the holding position, and then moves the latch to the over-center position. The coupled cam ring advances all jaw carriages until the pivoting pads seat on the pipe. To remove the clamp, releasing the latch unloads the spring stack and the carriage springs retract the jaws before the frame halves are opened.

The frame may carry a mounting boss outside the annular guide for supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit. The mounting boss does not participate in jaw synchronization. The disclosed essential relationship is that closure couples the ring segments and latch travel drives the coupled ring, while the oblique slots synchronize the radial jaw carriages and the force-limiting spring stack accommodates the remaining latch travel.

content.content:
1	In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame.
2	
3	Overall arrangement
4	
5	Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.
6	
7	Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame.
8	
9	The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.
10	
11	Jaw carriages and jaw pads
12	
13	Referring to FIGS. 2 and 5, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.
14	
15	Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.
16	
17	A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.
18	
19	The segmented cam ring
20	
21	A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.
22	
23	The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.
24	
25	The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.
26	
27	The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50. The first hinge-end drive face 44 and the second hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.
28	
29	The first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are shown in FIG. 6. In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.
30	
31	Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 5. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.
32	
33	The latch drive
34	
35	The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.
36	
37	The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.
38	
39	Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.
40	
41	Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.
42	
43	An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.
44	
45	Installation and removal
46	
47	To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.
48	
49	To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.
50	
51	The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.
52

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIGS. 2 and 5, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50. The first hinge-end drive face 44 and the second hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

The first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are shown in FIG. 6. In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 5. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

In the following description, like reference numerals designate like parts throughout the several views. The described arrangement is one form of the invention and is not a limitation on the scope of the claims. Terms of orientation such as inward, outward, radial and circumferential are used with reference to a central axis of the closed frame.

Overall arrangement

Referring to FIG. 1, a split pipe clamp 10 comprises a first frame half 12 and a second frame half 14. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are each substantially semicircular, and together they define a frame that surrounds a pipe 20 when closed. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are joined at a hinge end of the frame by a hinge 16 and are releasably joined at a latch end of the frame, opposite the hinge end, by a releasable latch 18. Swinging the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16 opens the frame laterally, so that the split pipe clamp 10 can be placed around the pipe 20. The split pipe clamp 10 and the pipe 20 together form an installed clamp assembly when the split pipe clamp 10 is closed and clamped on the pipe 20.

Three jaw carriages 22 are distributed circumferentially about the closed frame.

The frame carries a mounting boss 66. The mounting boss 66 supports a sensor, a tool or a conduit on the split pipe clamp 10. The mounting boss 66 does not participate in synchronizing the jaw carriages 22.

Jaw carriages and jaw pads

Referring to FIGS. 2 and 5, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. The radial guide 24 constrains the jaw carriage 22 to travel along a radial path toward and away from the central axis of the closed frame.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement and that presents a concave bearing surface toward the central axis of the closed frame. Because the jaw pad 26 pivots relative to the jaw carriage 22, the jaw pad 26 bears on the pipe 20 without requiring a tool specific pipe diameter.

A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward, away from the central axis of the closed frame. When the releasable latch 18 is released, the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22 outward and lift the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened.

The segmented cam ring

A cam ring 30 is retained in an annular guide 36 of the frame. The annular guide 36, shown in FIG. 2, retains the cam ring 30 while allowing the cam ring 30 to rotate through a limited stroke about the central axis of the closed frame.

The mounting boss 66 stands on the frame outside the annular guide 36.

The cam ring 30 is segmented. Referring to FIG. 3, the cam ring 30 comprises a first cam-ring segment 32 and a second cam-ring segment 34. The first cam-ring segment 32 is carried by the first frame half 12 and the second cam-ring segment 34 is carried by the second frame half 14, each segment being retained by the frame half that carries it. Each segment accordingly stays with its own frame half when the frame is opened, and the frame halves can be swung apart without dismantling the drive.

The first cam-ring segment 32 has a first hinge-end drive face 44 and a first latch-end drive face 48. The second cam-ring segment 34 has a second hinge-end drive face 46 and a second latch-end drive face 50. The first hinge-end drive face 44 and the second hinge-end drive face 46 are complementary to one another, and the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are complementary to one another. Closing the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 at the hinge end and brings the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50 at the latch end, and thereby couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 so that they rotate together as one cam ring 30 about the central axis of the closed frame.

The first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 are shown in FIG. 6. In the closed frame each pair of complementary drive faces transmits circumferential drive from one cam-ring segment to the other, and the complementary drive faces separate when the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are swung apart about the hinge 16.

Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 5. Each oblique slot 38 is inclined to the circumferential direction of the cam ring 30, so that rotation of the cam ring 30 through the limited stroke displaces the follower 40, and with it the jaw carriage 22, along the radial guide 24. The oblique slots 38 are arranged so that rotation of the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke produces the same inward travel at every jaw carriage 22. The inward travel of the three jaw carriages 22 is thereby synchronized.

The latch drive

The releasable latch 18 carries a wedge 52, as shown in FIG. 4. Moving the releasable latch 18 drives the wedge 52 against a ring drive face 54 of the cam ring 30, shown in FIG. 3, and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke.

The releasable latch 18 has a first position and a second position. In the first position the releasable latch 18 holds the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 around the pipe 20 without clamping the pipe 20. The second position is an over-center position, in which the releasable latch 18 has driven the wedge 52 and the cam ring 30 and clamps the pipe 20.

Referring again to FIG. 4, the releasable latch 18 comprises a latch handle 56, a latch housing 58 and a force-limiting spring stack 62. The force-limiting spring stack 62 lies in a drive path between the latch handle 56 and the wedge 52.

Once all of the jaw pads 26 have contacted the pipe 20, further movement of the latch handle 56 toward the over-center position compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62 rather than forcing one jaw pad 26 farther than the others. The latch travel that remains after contact is therefore taken up by the force-limiting spring stack 62.

An indicator pin 64 is visible on the releasable latch 18 and moves relative to a fixed edge 60 of the latch housing 58 when the force-limiting spring stack 62 enters a predetermined compression range. The position of the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60 is a mechanical report that the split pipe clamp 10 is loaded within that range. The indicator pin 64 reports clamp loading and does not measure the diameter of the pipe 20.

Installation and removal

To install the split pipe clamp 10, an operator opens the releasable latch 18 and swings the first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 apart about the hinge 16. The operator places the frame halves around the pipe 20 and closes them, which brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46 and the first latch-end drive face 48 into engagement with the second latch-end drive face 50, and so couples the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 into a single cam ring 30. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the first position, in which the frame halves are held around the pipe 20 without clamping. The operator then moves the releasable latch 18 to the over-center position. The wedge 52 bears on the ring drive face 54 and rotates the coupled cam ring 30 through the limited stroke, the oblique slots 38 advance all of the jaw carriages 22 inward together, and the jaw pads 26 pivot and seat on the pipe 20. Latch travel remaining after the jaw pads 26 seat compresses the force-limiting spring stack 62, and the operator observes the indicator pin 64 relative to the fixed edge 60.

To remove the split pipe clamp 10, the operator releases the releasable latch 18. The force-limiting spring stack 62 unloads and the carriage springs 42 retract the jaw carriages 22, lifting the jaw pads 26 off the pipe 20 before the frame halves are opened. The first frame half 12 and the second frame half 14 are then swung apart about the hinge 16, and the first hinge-end drive face 44, the second hinge-end drive face 46, the first latch-end drive face 48 and the second latch-end drive face 50 separate so that the first cam-ring segment 32 and the second cam-ring segment 34 travel with their own frame halves. The split pipe clamp 10 is reusable.

The essential relationship of the arrangement described here is that closure of the frame halves couples the cam-ring segments, that travel of the releasable latch 18 drives the coupled cam ring 30, that the oblique slots 38 synchronize the radial travel of the jaw carriages 22, and that the force-limiting spring stack 62 accommodates the remaining latch travel. The features described above may be combined in ways other than those expressly set out, and modifications within the understanding of a person skilled in the art fall within the scope of the claims that follow.

1	Pipework in process plants, buildings, vehicles and drilling installations often has to be gripped by a device that cannot be threaded on from a free end of the pipe. Sensors, monitoring heads, marking tools, small actuators and conduit supports are attached to a run of pipe that is already installed. A clamp intended for that duty is therefore built as a split clamp: a frame that opens, is placed around the pipe transversely, and is closed again.
2	
3	A split frame presents a mechanical problem that a one piece collar does not have, because the tightening motion has to be delivered to a frame that is divided. Where the grip is obtained by drawing the two frame halves toward one another so that the frame itself shrinks onto the pipe, the closing force enters the frame at the split line, and the grip that results depends on the closure hardware and on how far the halves have been drawn together.
4	
5	Where instead the frame is fitted with jaws that are advanced against the pipe one at a time, the grip is taken away from the split line, but the jaws have to be balanced against one another by the operator. If one jaw is advanced further than the others, the pipe is pushed away from the axis of the frame, and the clamp is seated differently each time it is fitted.
6	
7	A clamp whose jaw faces match one nominal pipe diameter also obliges a technician to select the clamp to suit the pipe before working, and a jaw face of fixed curvature meets a pipe of a different diameter along an edge rather than over an area.
8	
9	An operator working with a quick acting latch further has little indication of how hard the clamp has been applied. The latch closes to the same position whether the jaws have only just reached the pipe or have been driven hard against it, so the feel of the latch does not report the load the clamp is carrying, and a reading of pipe diameter reports only the size of the pipe.
10	
11	There is accordingly a need for a split pipe clamp that can be fitted by hand around an in place pipe over a range of diameters, that advances several jaws onto the pipe together rather than one at a time, and that reports mechanically to the operator when the clamping load has reached the intended range.
12

Sensors, monitoring heads, marking tools, small actuators and conduit supports are attached to a run of pipe that is already installed. A clamp intended for that duty is therefore built as a split clamp: a frame that opens, is placed around the pipe transversely, and is closed again.

A split frame presents a mechanical problem that a one piece collar does not have, because the tightening motion has to be delivered to a frame that is divided. Where the grip is obtained by drawing the two frame halves toward one another so that the frame itself shrinks onto the pipe, the closing force enters the frame at the split line, and the grip that results depends on the closure hardware and on how far the halves have been drawn together.

Where instead the frame is fitted with jaws that are advanced against the pipe one at a time, the grip is taken away from the split line, but the jaws have to be balanced against one another by the operator. If one jaw is advanced further than the others, the pipe is pushed away from the axis of the frame, and the clamp is seated differently each time it is fitted.

A clamp whose jaw faces match one nominal pipe diameter also obliges a technician to select the clamp to suit the pipe before working, and a jaw face of fixed curvature meets a pipe of a different diameter along an edge rather than over an area.

An operator working with a quick acting latch further has little indication of how hard the clamp has been applied. The latch closes to the same position whether the jaws have only just reached the pipe or have been driven hard against it, so the feel of the latch does not report the load the clamp is carrying, and a reading of pipe diameter reports only the size of the pipe.

There is accordingly a need for a split pipe clamp that can be fitted by hand around an in place pipe over a range of diameters, that advances several jaws onto the pipe together rather than one at a time, and that reports mechanically to the operator when the clamping load has reached the intended range.

content.text:
All four review findings are fixed; the claims, description body, numeral table, and background are untouched apart from one cross-reference.

**What changed**

- `figures/FIG-4.md`: the view now shows a short arcuate cam-ring portion visible through the break beneath the latch housing, with a short plain drive face on it and the lower end of the wedge bearing on that face. Numeral 54 added to the front matter, the placement targets, and the numerals list (8 numerals, at the sheet cap, so cam ring 30 was deliberately not added). The brief was tightened to 2786 characters to stay under the 2800 limit.
- `figures/FIG-3.md`: all three oblique slots are now required to be inclined in the same sense relative to the band, and the drive face is located in the latch-end region adjacent the right junction (FIG. 1 fixes hinge left, latch right) instead of being expressly unconstrained.
- `figures/FIG-6.md`: slots tied to the FIG. 3 positions and inclinations, same sense of inclination.
- `figures/FIG-5.md`: carriage spring now acts between the carriage and frame structure beside the slideway with its line of action radial, replacing the anchor on a slideway side line that could not react the outward bias.
- `draft/07-drawings.md`: FIG. 4 sentence now recites the wedge bearing on the ring drive face.
- `draft/08-detailed-description.md`: ring drive face 54 is now "shown in FIGS. 3 and 4", matching the sheets.

I did not run the render/OCR pipeline; figure files are Markdown specifications only, so drawing regeneration and the pixel-level gates happen downstream of these briefs.

input.summary: Resolved all four reviewer findings, every one of them an internal-consistency defect in the figure briefs, without touching the claims, the numeral table, the background, or the substance of the detailed description. FIG. 4 now depicts the claimed wedge-to-ring-drive-face engagement: a short arcuate cam-ring portion is visible through the break beneath the latch housing, its upper side carrying a short plain drive face on which the lower end of the wedge bears, and numeral 54 was added to the FIG-4 front matter, placement targets, and numerals list. That brings FIG. 4 to eight numerals, which is the per-sheet cap, so I did not add cam ring 30 to the sheet and instead worded the Brief Description sentence as "the wedge bearing on the ring drive face" so that no part named as visible in FIG. 4 lacks a listed numeral. Adding the cam-ring portion pushed the FIG-4 brief to 3182 characters, over the 2800 limit, so I compressed redundant wording (repeated "within the housing", duplicated "shown schematically", and non-essential placement qualifiers) back down to 2786 characters while keeping every required body, contact, and occlusion. FIG. 3 and FIG. 6 now require all three oblique slots to be inclined in the same sense relative to the band, which is what makes one rotation of the coupled ring move all three carriages inward by the same amount as the description and claim 6 recite; no angle, taper, or direction of lean is stated. FIG. 3's drive face is now placed in the latch-end region adjacent the right junction, which FIG. 1 establishes as the latch end, so the renderer cannot put it where the latch-carried wedge could not reach it; FIG. 6 inherits that position by its existing cross-reference. The FIG. 5 carriage spring no longer anchors to a slideway side line that could not react the outward bias; it acts between the carriage and frame structure beside the slideway with its line of action radial. The only body-text edits are the FIG. 4 sentence in the Brief Description and a change of "shown in FIG. 3" to "shown in FIGS. 3 and 4" for ring drive face 54, both required to keep the text and the sheets in step. I did not run the render, OCR, leader, or endpoint gates: figure files are Markdown specifications only and image generation is downstream of these briefs, so those gates run on the regenerated sheets rather than in this workspace.
reasoning: The wedge-to-drive-face finding was correct and the fix adds no unsupported matter: the disclosure states in terms that closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring, so depicting that contact is depiction of disclosed structure, not new structure. I placed the cam-ring portion where the FIG-4 brief already put a break in the frame band at the latch end, so it is visible without inventing a new cutaway.

FIG. 4 hit the eight-numeral cap once 54 was added. Rather than crowd a ninth numeral (30) onto the sheet or split off another detail view for a relationship that FIG. 3 already carries, I removed the words 'of the cam ring' from the FIG. 4 sentence in the Brief Description. The engagement is still expressly stated there, and every part the sentence names as shown has a numeral listed on the sheet.

The same-sense slot inclination is a consequence of the disclosed synchronized inward travel of all three carriages, not an added geometric fact. I stated only the common sense of inclination and left angle, lean direction, and slot proportions unspecified, so the brief still asserts nothing the inventor did not disclose.

The drive-face position follows from the disclosed drive path: the wedge is carried by the releasable latch, the latch is at the latch end, so the face the wedge bears on lies in the latch-end region. FIG. 1 already fixes hinge left and latch right, and FIG. 6 already numbers the latch-end drive faces at the right junction, so 'adjacent the right junction' is consistent across all three sheets rather than a new choice.

The FIG. 5 spring anchor was genuinely self-contradictory: a spring reacting against a line parallel to the direction of travel cannot bias the carriage along that direction. The disclosure supports only that a spring biases each carriage outward, so I kept the radial line of action and dropped the anchor detail rather than inventing a reaction seat.

content.text:
I read the gate report against the briefs and the draft. All six failures are drawing-side; nothing in the specification text, claims, or numeral table is implicated, so those files are untouched byte for byte.

Two distinct defect classes:

**Figure label OCR (FIG. 1, 3, 4, 5).** The rendered caption is being read as the stray text `FIG` plus a loose digit, which trips both the "unexpected numeral" and "wrong figure label" checks. Each brief now pins the sheet lettering: one centered single-line label containing the period and one space, the label digit declared not to be a reference numeral, and nothing else lettered on the sheet.

**Geometry drift (FIG. 2, FIG. 6).** FIG. 2 rendered five slideways and carriages; FIG. 6 rendered a 3D perspective ring with four slots and junctions collapsed to single shared lines, so 44/46/48/50 had nothing distinct to point at. The briefs now state exact counts with explicit clock positions (top, lower right, lower left — clear of the left and right breaks), forbid perspective/isometric projection in FIG. 6, and draw each junction as two side-by-side lines with a narrow clearance so each end face is its own identifiable geometry carrying its own leader. The clearance is labeled a depiction convention; the faces still abut in use, exactly as the disclosure and the detailed description say.

Nothing about the invention changed — the counts I made explicit are the three jaw carriages and three oblique slots already recited in the disclosure, claims, and description. No slot, face, or feature was added to match what the image model drew.

Note on the record as a whole: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art on file may be incomplete. Also, `input/conversation.md` contains a prior drafting-agent statement describing "a self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" as the point of novelty; that feature appears nowhere in the disclosure or in this draft, and I treated it as stray text rather than authority.

FIG-2 rendered five slideways and carriages instead of three, so the brief now requires exactly three, no more and no fewer, at equal angular intervals of about one third of a turn at named positions (top, lower right, lower left) clear of both breaks, with exactly three carriages, one per slideway. FIG-6 rendered a 3D perspective ring with four slots and junctions drawn as single shared lines, leaving 44, 46, 48 and 50 with no distinct geometry to label; the brief now requires a flat two-dimensional face-on view in the plane of the sheet with true circles and no perspective, isometric or oblique projection, exactly three slots at the same positions as FIG. 3, and each junction drawn as two side-by-side plain lines with a narrow clearance so the end face of the upper segment and the end face of the lower segment are separately identifiable and each carries its own lead line. FIG-3 was given the same explicit slot count and positions so that FIG-6's "same positions as FIG. 3" resolves to one unambiguous layout. The narrow junction clearance is stated in the brief as a depiction convention only; the drive faces still abut when the frame is closed, as the disclosure and the detailed description recite. No feature, count or implementation detail was added to accommodate anything the image model drew. Note for the file: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art on hand may be incomplete; separately, input/conversation.md contains a prior agent statement about "a self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" that has no support in the disclosure and appears nowhere in this draft, and it was disregarded.

structured_output.summary: Repaired all six failing drawing sheets by amending only the authoritative Markdown figure briefs; no rendered artifact was touched and no specification, claim, or numeral-table text was altered. FIG-1, FIG-3, FIG-4 and FIG-5 failed OCR label review ("unexpected <digit>; other text FIG; wrong figure label"), so each brief now pins the sheet lettering to a single centered line reading exactly "FIG. n" with the period and one space, declares the label digit not to be a reference numeral, and forbids any other lettering. FIG-2 rendered five slideways and carriages instead of three, so the brief now requires exactly three, no more and no fewer, at equal angular intervals of about one third of a turn at named positions (top, lower right, lower left) clear of both breaks, with exactly three carriages, one per slideway. FIG-6 rendered a 3D perspective ring with four slots and junctions drawn as single shared lines, leaving 44, 46, 48 and 50 with no distinct geometry to label; the brief now requires a flat two-dimensional face-on view in the plane of the sheet with true circles and no perspective, isometric or oblique projection, exactly three slots at the same positions as FIG. 3, and each junction drawn as two side-by-side plain lines with a narrow clearance so the end face of the upper segment and the end face of the lower segment are separately identifiable and each carries its own lead line. FIG-3 was given the same explicit slot count and positions so that FIG-6's "same positions as FIG. 3" resolves to one unambiguous layout. The narrow junction clearance is stated in the brief as a depiction convention only; the drive faces still abut when the frame is closed, as the disclosure and the detailed description recite. No feature, count or implementation detail was added to accommodate anything the image model drew. Note for the file: no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art on hand may be incomplete; separately, input/conversation.md contains a prior agent statement about "a self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" that has no support in the disclosure and appears nowhere in this draft, and it was disregarded.

patches.replace: View: enlarged view of the segmented cam ring of FIG. 3, drawn as one single view at one scale and at a larger scale than FIG. 3, showing the end faces that abut one another at the two junctions between the segments. The view is a flat two-dimensional face-on view lying in the plane of the sheet, exactly the same kind of view as FIG. 3 and differing from it only in scale. There is no perspective, no isometric or oblique projection, no three-dimensional body, no wall thickness, no depth, and no visible side, rim or edge surface of the ring. Every circle on the sheet is a true circle and never an ellipse, and every junction line is a straight line lying in the plane of the sheet. Patent line drawing, black line work on white, no shading or color.
patches.why: Semantic review failed this sheet twice for being drawn as a 3D perspective view where the brief calls for two concentric circles. Naming the excluded projections explicitly, and tying the view to FIG. 3 as differing only in scale, closes the reading that produced the perspective render.

patches.find:
- At the left junction the end of the upper segment and the end of the lower segment terminate in complementary end faces that abut one another, the junction drawn as a single plain line across the full width of the band. The end faces are shown schematically.
- At the right junction the other end of the upper segment and the other end of the lower segment terminate in complementary end faces that abut one another in the same way, drawn as a single plain line across the full width of the band. The end faces are shown schematically.
patches.replace:
- At the left junction the end of the upper segment and the end of the lower segment terminate in complementary end faces that abut one another. At the enlarged scale of this view each of those two end faces is drawn as its own plain straight line across the full width of the band, the two lines lying side by side across the band with a narrow clearance between them, the upper line being the end face of the upper segment and the lower line being the end face of the lower segment. The two end faces are therefore two separate, individually identifiable pieces of line work and not one shared line, and each can receive its own lead line. The narrow clearance is a depiction convention adopted so that the two end faces read separately at this scale; the end faces abut one another when the frame halves are closed. The end faces are shown schematically.
- At the right junction the other end of the upper segment and the other end of the lower segment terminate in complementary end faces that abut one another in the same way. Each of those two end faces is again drawn as its own plain straight line across the full width of the band, the two lines lying side by side with the same narrow clearance between them, the upper line being the end face of the upper segment and the lower line being the end face of the lower segment, so that each of these two end faces is likewise separately identifiable and can receive its own lead line. The end faces are shown schematically.
patches.why: Semantic review found that parts 44, 46, 48 and 50 are 'not shown as distinct, individually identifiable geometries; the junctions are depicted as simple lines', which is also why the four numerals came back missing. Giving each end face its own line supplies four leader endpoints without inventing any structure: the faces remain plain, complementary and abutting exactly as the disclosure and draft/08-detailed-description.md state, and the clearance is declared a depiction convention.

patches.find: - Three elongated slots through the band, in the same positions and at the same inclinations as in FIG. 3, all inclined in the same sense relative to the band. The slots are shown schematically and carry no numeral on this sheet.

patches.why: Semantic review found four slots where three are required. The count and the named positions now match the amended FIG. 3 and the three oblique slots recited in the claims and detailed description.

content.content:
1	# Invention disclosure (the inventor's own words)
2	
3	This is the ONLY authority for what the invention includes. Everything you claim must be supported here or in later messages from the user.
4	
5	A reusable split pipe clamp has a first semicircular frame half and a second semicircular frame half joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end. Three radial jaw carriages are distributed around the closed frame. Each carriage slides in a radial guide and carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe without requiring a tool-specific pipe diameter.
6	
7	A segmented cam ring is retained in an annular guide of the frame. One cam-ring segment is carried by each frame half. When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring. Each jaw carriage has a follower received in a respective oblique slot of the cam ring. Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring and rotates the coupled ring through a limited stroke. The oblique slots translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages. A spring biases each carriage outward when the latch is released.
8	
9	The latch has a first position that holds the frame halves around the pipe without clamping and a second over-center position that drives the cam ring and clamps the pipe. A force-limiting spring stack lies between the latch handle and the wedge, so additional handle travel after all jaw pads contact the pipe compresses the spring stack rather than forcing one jaw farther than the others. A visible indicator pin moves relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing when the spring stack enters a predetermined compression range. The indicator reports clamp loading mechanically and does not measure pipe diameter.
